keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 7 grid cells (about 1,800 km2 by the gazetteer); the page: 'In 1969, the 100 occupied islands comprised 700 square miles (1,800 km2)' (ratio 1.0), with 3,000,000 square miles of sea. Guam is not in the territory.

correction.text: Palau alone: after the Marshall Islands (21 October 1986), Micronesia and the Marianas (3 November 1986) 'Palau' remained a trust territory to 1 October 1994

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Palau district only, one grid cell (the main group; Peleliu, Angaur, Kayangel and Sonsorol are below the grid). The Security Council ended the trusteeship for the other districts on 22 December 1990 and for Palau on 25 May 1994.

region.text: the Marshall, Mariana and Caroline Islands and Palau

ledger.note: 1947: the United States takes the former Japanese mandate as a UN strategic trust: 'The TTPI entered UN trusteeship pursuant to Security Council Resolution 21 on July 18, 1947.' The Navy governed it from a headquarters in Guam.
1951: the Interior Department replaces the Navy and the seat moves from Guam to Saipan: 'The United States Navy controlled the TTPI from a headquarters in Guam until 1951.'
1986: the Marshall Islands leave the trust territory: 'On October 21, 1986, the US ended its administration of the Marshall Islands District' (Compact of Free Association effective 21 October 1986).

region.text: the Chuuk, Yap, Kosrae and Pohnpei districts

ledger.note: 1986: Chuuk, Yap, Kosrae and Pohnpei leave the trust territory on 3 November 1986: 'Chuuk, Yap, Kosrae, Pohnpei, and the Mariana Islands districts of the TTPI soon followed on November 3, 1986' (COFA effective 3 November 1986 for the Federated States of Micronesia).

1986: the Mariana Islands district leaves on 3 November 1986 to become the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (constitution 'partially effective January 1, 1978, and fully effective November 4, 1986').

1994: Palau becomes independent. The Security Council ended Palau's trusteeship on 25 May 1994 and 'the US and Palau agreed to establish the latter's independence on October 1' (COFA effective 1 October 1994).

region.text: the Palau District, the last district

ledger.note: 1994: the last trust territory of the United Nations ends with Palau's independence on 1 October 1994. The Security Council had formally ended the trusteeship for the other districts on 22 December 1990 (Resolution 683).

certainty.note: Island territory: the border is the coast and the district boundaries of the trusteeship; the free-association relations after 1986 are not territory.

sources.title: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands
sources.note: Resolution 21 of 18 July 1947; Navy headquarters in Guam to 1951, Interior from Saipan; six districts; Marshalls 21 October 1986, Micronesia and Marianas 3 November 1986, Palau 1 October 1994; Resolution 683 on 22 December 1990; area 1,800 km2 in 1969.

notes:
Written by oc-02-x. Pages used: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands, South Seas Mandate (1947 revocation). The page was thin on the budget: no Security Council date of 2 April 1947 (the Resolution 21 date is 18 July 1947), no 1962 date, no nuclear testing detail.
MODEL. A colony dossier of the United States (family americas, the US colour family), 7 cells at its fullest. After 1986 the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia and Palau are in 'free association' with the United States; the page lists COFA effective dates but the dossier treats the exit from the trust territory as the end of US governance, as oc-02-b's micronesia and palau dossiers start at those dates. Whether the free-association states are drawn as a US tint is the US dossier's decision (am-07).
SUCCESSOR DOSSIERS (written later in this run by oc-02-x). The Marshall Islands (republic-of-the-marshall-islands, 21 October 1986; the 1979 constitution is not on this page) and the Northern Mariana Islands (commonwealth-of-the-northern-mariana-islands, 1978 and 4 November 1986) have no Cliopatria row; both now have a dossier. The Security Council ended the trusteeship for six districts on 22 December 1990 (Resolution 683) and for Palau on 25 May 1994. Cliopatria's United States row (am-07) still contains Pohnpei and Palau's main cell to 2005 (oc-02-b's note).
NOT ON THE PAGE. The Marianas covenant of 1975 to 1978, the nuclear-test atolls (Bikini, Enewetak, Kwajalein), the 1962 transfer to the Interior Department's civilian administration, Hawaii as a headquarters.
